title: Riot Platforms Names Anthropic as Tenant for $28B Texas AI Campus
summary:
The operator of the Corsicana campus has disclosed that its latest land-lease agreement for 910 MW of power capacity is with Anthropic, the creator of the Claude AI assistant. The 15 year deal for the Texas facility is valued at about $28B, marking the largest lease in the history of Riot Platforms and bringing the company's total contracted data center revenue to approximately $38B.

Riot reported third-quarter revenue of $181.4M, beating analyst estimates of $161M, although net income fell to $4.03M from $104.5M in the same period last year. To finance its transition into AI infrastructure, the miner sold 20,264 bitcoin for roughly $1.5B during the first nine months of 2026, which reduced its bitcoin holdings from 18,005 at the start of the year to 2,418 by the end of September.

selectedTweets.bestBit: RIOT's expected capital requirement is just $6MM/MW, reflecting $2MM/MW for site work and electrical infrastructure, and $4MM/MW in reimbursements to Anthropic
selectedTweets.text:
The Riot $RIOT - Anthropic "powered land lease" deal at Riot's Corsicana site might have just set the new high watermark for AI/HPC lease economics. Unlike the build-to-suit structures seen in the vast majority of prior transactions, RIOT is simply renting Anthropic access to its powered land, and isn't required to build the data center itself:

"The lease is structured as a triple-net powered land lease, under which Riot delivers the land, the power infrastructure, and the powered pads, while continuing to own and maintain the high- and medium-voltage infrastructure that will serve them." - per RIOT 8-K

RIOT's expected capital requirement is just $6MM/MW, reflecting $2MM/MW for site work and electrical infrastructure, and $4MM/MW in reimbursements to Anthropic (e.g. help fund Anthropic's construction capex).

So in exchange for simply procuring and assembling the site's electrical infrastructure at an expected cost of $1.8 billion.. plus funding $3.6 billion of tenant reimbursements.. so an "all-in" cost of ~$5.5 billion.. RIOT receives $28 billion in rent over a 15-year period, or roughly $1.8 billion per year on average.. 

RIOT's expected year 1 (e.g. 2027-2028) NOI per MW of $1.6MM implies a 27% unlevered yield on cost. 

RIOT's expected average annual NOI per MW of $2MM/MW implies a 33% unlevered yield on cost. 

Previous leases have seen landlords collect $2MM/MW in rent.. but those landlords had to incur $12MM/MW+ in capex costs. RIOT is getting $2 million/MW for just $6MM/MW in capex. Insane.
